:::{#lem-loocv-not-random}
#### Leave-one-out cross-validation does not depend on the fold assignment

In $k$-fold cross-validation with $k = n$ [folds](#def-folds),
each fold holds exactly one observation,
so the [fold-out rule](#def-fold-out-rule) $\fittedwo{\foldof{i}}{\cdot}$
of observation $i$ is fitted to all observations except observation $i$,
whichever [fold assignment](#def-fold-assignment) $\foldof{i}$ is used.
Every assignment therefore gives the same
[cross-validation estimate](#def-cv-estimate) (@eq-cv-estimate with $k = n$),
the same $n$ fits with the folds numbered differently:

$$
\cvest{n} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i \in I} \sqf{\fittedwo{\foldof{i}}{x_i} - y_i}.
$$

:::

::: proof
This is the solution to @exr-loocv, part 3, worked in @sol-loocv.
It uses @eq-cv-estimate and @eq-fold-out-rule.
:::
